Title: Standard One pupil dies after falling from 10th floor of PPR
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 7-year-old pupil died after he was believed to have fallen from the 10th floor of a People's Housing Project (PPR) in Tampoi here today.
The incident occurred around 5.30pm while the boy was riding his bicycle outside his home.
At the time, his mother was inside the house, while his father, who works as a lorry attendant, was away at work.
The boy's mother was informed of the incident by one of his friends. The victim was the second of four siblings.
A check at the scene found a police forensic team conducting investigations, including seizing the boy's bicycle for further examination.
The boy's body was sent to Hospital Sultanah Aminah here for a post-mortem.
The New Straits Times have reached out to the police for comments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Two men filmed riding on roof of moving Proton Wira
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two men were filmed sitting on the roof of a moving Proton Wira, appearing unfazed as the car travelled along the road in a stunt that has drawn criticism on social media.
The
video, believed to have been recorded
by a motorist travelling behind the car, showed a third person driving while the two men sat on the roof.
The person recording the footage could be heard reading out the car's registration number and mentioning the location where the incident allegedly occurred.
At one point, the Wira slowed down as it approached a speed breaker, leaving the two men struggling to maintain their balance.
Despite the obvious risk of falling, they appeared carefree as the vehicle continued moving.
The footage was later shared on Facebook, where it garnered more than 20,000 views and over 200 comments.
Many users criticised the men's behaviour, with some describing it as "jakun" and questioning why anyone would risk their own lives and those of other road users for what appeared to be a stunt.
The incident has also raised concerns over road safety, given the risks posed by travelling in positions that offer no protection in the event of sudden braking or a collision.
It is unclear when and where the footage was recorded, or whether any action has been taken against those involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tree branch crushes lorry cab, driver escapes unhurt
Article:
BATU KAWAN: A lorry driver escaped unhurt after a tree branch crashed onto the prime mover near Masjid Ar-Rayyan in Bandar Cassia today.
The Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call regarding the incident along Jalan Batu Kawan at 2.10pm.
It is understood that the fallen branch, originating from a 20-foot Acacia tree with a circumference of 2.5m, crushed the front portion of the vehicle.
Rescuers confirmed that the 42-year-old lorry driver escaped unharmed from the ordeal.
A team of eight firefighters from the Batu Kawan fire and rescue station was dispatched to the scene to carry out clearing operations.
They used cutting equipment, with assistance from personnel and machinery from a neighbouring fire station and the Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP).
The operation was called off at 3.51pm after the team ensured the road was safe for motorists.

Title: Two Japanese climbers die on remote Himalayan peak in Nepal
Article:
KATHMANDU: Rescuers recovered the bodies on Friday of two Japanese climbers missing for over a week on a remote Himalayan mountain, an expedition organiser said.
The climbers were attempting the first summit of the 7,140-metre (23,425-foot) Gangapurna West in alpine style, but lost contact after Oct 15.
Kumar Chhetri of Cosmo Adventure, which offered the climbers logistical support, said the search began after they failed to return to basecamp on Oct 18 as planned.
"The rescue team this morning spotted the bodies at an altitude of around 6,300 metres," Chhetri told AFP.
He said the search team first spotted their camping spots and then a rucksack along with ropes a few days later.
"The bodies have been recovered and brought to Kathmandu. We are waiting for their family's decision for further action," he said.
Nepal sits in the Himalayas, and its mountains – which include Everest, the world's tallest – have long drawn climbers from across the world.
A growing community of mountaineers is exploring hidden summits promising solitude and the chance to be first to the top.
The country has 462 peaks open for climbing, and about 100 have never been summited.

Title: Coffin, mock graves mark protest against 'killer road' on Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A series of accidents involving heavy vehicles, including a 12-vehicle pile-up that injured four people earlier this month, has renewed calls for urgent safety improvements along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari.
More than 100 residents from Alam Budiman and neighbouring housing areas staged a protest at the Jalan Alam Budiman traffic junction today, highlighting what they described as a "killer road".
Carrying a replica coffin and placing mock graves at the intersection, they called on the authorities to address recurring accidents and expedite a proposed 5km flyover project, which they said had been mooted 15 years ago.
Gabungan Penduduk U10 residents' association chairman Badrul Hisham Shahbudin said the proposed flyover was needed to accommodate growing traffic volumes and improve safety for motorists from Puncak Alam, Puncak Perdana, Meru, Saujana Utama and surrounding areas.
"We hope the proposed flyover will be given serious attention as this is a main route for motorists from these areas to access Dash.
"We have been calling for road widening and the construction of a flyover for years because we believe these are the solutions needed. However, we still want to know when the project will be implemented," he said after the protest.
Greenhill Residence chairman Mohd Zailani Johari, 57, called for immediate safety measures rather than leaving residents to wait for the proposed flyover.
He said the recent accidents involving heavy vehicles had heightened fear and trauma among residents.
"Residents want safety measures to be implemented immediately because we cannot simply wait for the flyover to be built while road users continue to face risks every day.
"We hope the authorities will review the road conditions and introduce improvements in the near future," he said.
Their protest follows a series of crashes along the route this month, including an incident on Oct 9 in which a lorry crashed into 11 other vehicles at the Alam Budiman traffic lights, injuring four people.
Two victims, a man and a woman, suffered serious head injuries, while two other men sustained minor injuries.
Police later confirmed that the
51-year-old lorry driver
had tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
Based on preliminary investigations, the driver claimed that his vehicle suffered brake failure while travelling downhill from Puncak Perdana towards Puncak Alam, causing him to lose control.
On Oct 16, another accident involving several vehicles occurred at Kilometre 9.2 of Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari.
A four-wheel-drive vehicle reportedly hit the rear of a lorry before its driver lost control and veered into the opposite lane, colliding with another lorry and a car.
Three days later, a lorry carrying gravel overturned near the entrance to the Alam Budiman business centre after its driver reportedly lost control while travelling downhill.
The driver was
trapped in the wreckage
before being rescued.
On Oct 21, the
Selangor Public Works Department
announced plans to add a 300m lane from Puncak Alam towards Shah Alam at the Alam Budiman junction, alongside additional street lighting, traffic light upgrades and other safety improvements.
Preliminary works were under way, with physical construction expected to begin in mid-2027, according to a report published on Oct 22.
The proposed improvements are aimed at easing congestion and improving safety along the route, which serves several rapidly growing residential areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Rauf wants BN, Pas to work together, set aside prejudice
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) election machinery in Melaka must set aside any reservations about Pas and work with the party on the ground.
State BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all party machinery should accept the cooperation agreed upon by the parties' leadership and ensure it was reflected in their campaign efforts.
"The decision to cooperate with Pas has been made, and I urge all our machinery to work together with Pas without prejudice," he said after launching the BN election machinery for the Pantai Kundor state constituency here today.
Also present were Pantai Kundor incumbent Datuk Tuminah Kadi and Melaka MCA chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong.
Rauf, who is also caretaker Melaka chief minister, said the state election would be important in determining the state's direction and gauging the coalition's strength ahead of the next general election.
"Insya-Allah, if we succeed in Melaka, we can make it to Putrajaya. This is also a step towards the general election," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hamzah tells Kelantan Bersatu leaders to respect PN leadership
Article:
KOTA BARU: Bersatu leaders in Kelantan should respect Perikatan Nasional's (PN) leadership and abide by its decisions.
Comparing PN to a team, Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said its members should follow the captain's lead rather than act independently.
"If we are in the same team, we must follow the captain's lead. We already have a captain.
"If anyone disagrees with the captain and wants to do things their own way, they should consider leaving the team," he told reporters here today.
Hamzah said Wawasan and Pas Kelantan had discussed political cooperation and preparations for the 16th General Election (GE16), including Wawasan's electoral prospects in the state.
He said the talks covered broader political developments and cooperation within PN, rather than focusing solely on seat allocation in Kelantan.
Hamzah had met Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and Pas Kelantan commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yakob to discuss matters of mutual interest.
He said the discussions had gone well and would not affect Wawasan's cooperation with the Pas-led state government.
"Insya-Allah, there is nothing that will affect our cooperation with the Pas-led state government, particularly within PN," he said.
Hamzah said the talks also touched on Kelantan's political landscape, where Wawasan had won seats in the previous state election.
He said the parties had discussed their future political direction but left it to the Menteri Besar to assess the situation and decide on the best course of action.
"We discussed various matters, but I leave it to the Menteri Besar to assess the situation as we do not want to disrupt anything," he said.
He added that Wawasan's preparations for GE16 extended beyond Kelantan, with the party taking into account the wider political landscape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media Council warns against identifying minors in incident reports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) wants media organisations to refrain from publishing details or unverified social media content that could directly or indirectly identify children involved in incidents as suspects, victims or witnesses.
In a statement, it reminded newsrooms that under Clause 9.3 of its Code of Conduct, the interests of children under 18 must be protected and may only be overridden where there is an exceptional public benefit.
"Information that attracts public attention does not necessarily serve the public interest," it said.
MMC acknowledged that incidents involving minors, particularly in schools, were matters of legitimate public concern. However, it said, it must be balanced against the potential harm to the children involved.
Under Clause 4.3, the names, photographs and identifiable locations of juvenile suspects or persons of interest must not be published or broadcast, it said.
MMC also cautioned that details such as a child's age, class, family background and social media accounts could indirectly reveal their identity.
"Materials circulating on social media and messaging platforms, including personal notes, messages, screenshots, photographs and videos allegedly involving or originating from a minor, must not be presented as established facts without appropriate verification of their source and authenticity," MMC said.
It added that under Clause 1.6, unverified information may only be reported where there is a clear public benefit, reasonable attempts at verification have been made, and the information is clearly identified as unverified.
"Such reporting must not be accompanied by speculation or misleading conclusions," it said.
MMC urged newsrooms to respect the presumption of innocence, avoid sensationalism, show compassion when interviewing affected families, and review and correct past coverage that breached the Code.
Members of the public affected by media coverage that may have breached the Code can lodge complaints through MMC's Grievance Mechanism.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak election dates to be decided at special EC meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting to decide key dates for the Sarawak election after receiving official notification of the state assembly from its Speaker.
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the meeting date had yet to be fixed and would be announced later.
"We will wait for official notification from the Speaker before setting the relevant dates, taking into account various factors to ensure the smooth conduct of the election," he told Bernama.
On preparations, Khairul Shahril said the EC had begun making logistical arrangements, preparing equipment, training election personnel and identifying suitable polling centres.
On the EC's readiness, he said preliminary preparations included logistical arrangements, equipment supplies, training for election personnel and identifying suitable locations for polling centres.
"In terms of logistics, training and personnel, we are ready," he said.
He added that a proposal to use Optical Character Recognition-Voters Attendance (OCR-VA) technology in the state election would be submitted to EC members for evaluation before a decision was made.
Earlier today, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the
state assembly would be dissolved
effective Oct 26, paving the way for the 13th state election.
He said the decision was made after obtaining the consent of Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak polls: Wawasan to discuss election plans with PN
Article:
KOTA BHARU: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) will discuss its direction for the Sarawak election with Perikatan Nasional (PN) before deciding whether to contest.
Its president, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin, said the party had members in Sarawak but would not make a decision unilaterally.
"We have members there, as does Pas. However, whether we contest or not, we should discuss it with PN rather than decide on our own.
"We will wait for the PN discussion," he told a press conference here today.
The Sarawak State Legislative Assembly will be
dissolved
on Oct 26 to pave the way for the 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg announced this at Kompleks Satria Pertiwi in Petra Jaya today, after an audience with Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar at Astana Negeri.

Title: Zetrix AI fails to resolve RM2bil sukuk breach, offers 789mil share options
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has failed to reach an agreement with its sukukholders over a covenant breach involving its RM2 billion sukuk programme, prolonging uncertainty over the company's debt obligations.
The setback came as the embattled technology group offered nearly 789 million share options to directors and employees at a 28 per cent discount to its closing share price of 7.5 sen today.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Zetrix AI said no resolution was reached at today's sukukholders' meeting, which was convened to discuss a proposed arrangement to address the breach.
"There was no resolution achieved by all parties during the sukuk holders' meeting," it said.
The company said another meeting would be arranged, although no date had been fixed.
The discussions followed the expiry of the Oct 22 deadline to remedy the breach, which arose after forced share sales by banks reduced managing director Wong Thean Soon's combined direct and indirect stake to 1.895 per cent as at Oct 15.
Under the terms of its Sukuk Wakalah programme, Wong is required to remain the company's single largest shareholder.
Without a waiver or an acceptable resolution, Zetrix AI risks triggering a dissolution event that could allow the sukuk trustee to demand accelerated repayment of outstanding amounts.
The company has RM2 billion in outstanding sukuk principal and RM164.5 million in future coupon payments.
In a separate filing, Zetrix AI announced an offer of 788.83 million options under its employees' share option scheme at an exercise price of 5.4 sen each.
The options, which vested immediately, were offered to eligible directors and employees.
Wong was offered 27.5 million options, while chairman Datuk Dr Norraesah Mohamad and directors Datuk Mohd Jimmy Wong Abdullah and Wong Kok Chau were each offered 10 million options.
Together, the four directors were offered 57.5 million options.
Zetrix AI's shares surged 50 per cent to close at 7.5 sen today, after months of heavy selling driven by financial and governance concerns.
The group has faced mounting pressure in recent weeks, including a sharp credit rating downgrade and the withdrawal of its previously declared interim dividend to preserve working capital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court upholds lorry driver's 30-year jail term, 12 strokes for drug trafficking
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court today upheld the 30-year jail term and 12 strokes of the rotan imposed on a former lorry driver for trafficking 1.4645 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine.
A three-judge panel led by Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, together with Federal Court judges Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Azimah Omar, dismissed Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Hasnu's appeal against his conviction and sentence.
Delivering the court's unanimous decision, Che Mohd Ruzima said the High Court judge had correctly applied the presumption of knowledge under Section 37(d) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, and that the appellant (Fahmi) had failed to rebut the presumption.
"We find that the drugs were inside a bag, and the bag was in the possession and control of the appellant," he said, adding that the court rejected the defence's argument that the drugs had been found inside the car.
Che Mohd Ruzima said the court found that the drugs had not been discovered concealed in any part of the car driven by the appellant, but were found inside a bag on the right rear seat of the vehicle.
He said the court also gave weight to several key facts - the appellant was driving the car alone at the time of the incident, the bag was in a clearly visible location, and he was seen moving towards and reaching for the bag when the raid was conducted.
"Therefore, there is no reason for us to amend the conviction from trafficking to possession, as proposed by the appellant.
The appeal is dismissed, and the conviction and sentence imposed by the High Court and upheld by the Court of Appeal are maintained," he said.
The defence had argued that the High Court judge erred in invoking the presumption of knowledge under Section 37(d), contending that the presumption could not be applied to drugs found inside a vehicle because a vehicle did not fall within the definition of "anything whatsoever containing".
On May 13, 2024, the High Court found Fahmi, 39, guilty of trafficking 1.4645 kg of methamphetamine at the Rusella apartment complex in Taman Pinggiran Putra, Seri Kembangan, Selangor, at 6.45 pm on Oct 8, 2020.
On March 24 last year, the Court of Appeal dismissed Ahmad Fahmi's appeal and upheld the High Court's decision.
At today's proceedings, Ahmad Fahmi was represented by lawyer Afifuddin Ahmad Hafifi, while Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohd Zain Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix AI redesignates Norraesah from executive chairman to chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has redesignated Datuk Norraesah Mohamad from executive chairman to chairman.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company announced the change as part of its latest boardroom update.
The announcement did not specify the reason for the redesignation.
Norraesah, 78, has been associated with the company since August 18, 2006, according to its director profile.
She holds a PhD in economics from the University of Paris I, Pantheon-Sorbonne.
Before her corporate career, she served in the government, including at the then
International Trade and Industry Ministry and the Finance Ministry from 1972 to 1988.
She was also chairman of Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd from 2000 to 2003 and served as a senator from 2005 to 2008.

Title: Body of baby girl found in Bangsar rubbish bin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a baby girl, estimated to be around seven months old, was found at a waste disposal site in Bangsar here today.
Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the department received a report regarding the discovery of the baby in a rubbish bin at 10.43am.
"The baby's body was taken to the Forensics Unit of Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) for a post-mortem, and investigations are being conducted under Section 318 of the Penal Code," he said in a statement today.
Hoo urged anyone with information about the incident to come forward to assist in the investigation.
Information can be channelled via the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2115 9999, the Brickfields Police Hotline at 03-2297 9222, or by visiting any nearby police station. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN invited Bersatu to meeting as early as Sept 20, says Hamzah
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) had invited Bersatu to attend a supreme council meeting as early as Sept 20, but it was postponed due to a commitment involving the coalition chairman, said Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
The Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president said the invitation, extended after the High Court granted a stay on the suspension and deregistration of PN, was not the first time the coalition had invited Bersatu to the meeting.
Hamzah said Bersatu had the right to attend the meeting if they wished to do so.
"This is not the first time PN has invited Bersatu to a meeting. The first invitation was issued on Sept 20, but the meeting was postponed because the chairman had other commitments," he told reporters.
The invitation comes amid an internal dispute that threatened PN's status as a registered political coalition.
The dispute began after Bersatu lodged a complaint with the Registrar of Societies (RoS), alleging that it had been excluded from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16. The party also questioned its membership status within the coalition.
RoS confirmed receiving the complaint on Aug 11 before issuing a show-cause notice to PN on Sept 22, requiring it to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.
The following day, RoS suspended PN's activities under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966.
On Oct 20, RoS cancelled PN's registration under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the same Act.
Hamzah said PN had previously taken similar action against Parti Rakyat India Malaysia (MIPP) after receiving complaints about internal problems within the party.
He said a letter had been sent to MIPP asking it to resolve the issues, adding that the party would not be invited to meetings until they were settled.
"Before the meeting even started, MIPP had already said it received a letter. The same thing happened to Bersatu.
"If I were the secretary-general, I would do the same thing," he said.
Hamzah said PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, a lawyer, was expected to act in accordance with the law and regulations.
He said Takiyuddin should not be blamed for carrying out his duties according to the rules.
"He is a lawyer, so his job is to follow the law and regulations. This should be accepted positively," he said.
Yesterday, Takiyuddin said the coalition would
convene a meeting
soon following the High Court's decision to
grant a stay on the RoS action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police rule out foul play in fatal Kajang helium tank explosion
Article:
KAJANG: Police have ruled out foul play in a helium tank explosion that
killed
a 49-year-old worker at a scrap metal processing factory in Sungai Chua here today.
Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations found no criminal elements in the incident, which occurred at 12.22pm.
The victim was found unconscious with injuries to his left leg.
Naazron said police received a report on the incident at 12.58pm and rushed to the scene.
"The victim was pronounced dead by Kajang Hospital medical personnel, who arrived at the scene at 12.35pm," he said.
He said the victim's body was sent to Hospital Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
"The case has been classified as sudden death, pending further findings," he said, adding that investigations were ongoing to determine the cause of the explosion.
Those with information are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Shisheewady Ruzani at 016-856 5670 to assist in the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK tells public to keep three days' emergency supplies at home
Article:
LONDON: The British government advised the public on Friday to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, a message it said had been hammered home by this week's PHP software glitch, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires.
Governments and businesses worldwide have rushed to secure systems running the PHP programming language after flaws were disclosed on Wednesday, forcing some services offline and triggering millions of hacking attempts in one of the most significant cybersecurity incidents in recent years.
The British government said the internet outage showed the importance of its newly launched "Be Ready" campaign, which advises the public to keep three days of bottled water and non-perishable food in the house.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham, hosting a meeting on the response to wildfires, said that in the past Britain had been "on the back foot" responding to emergencies and that it needed to be more proactive.
The government announced a new wildfire response plan that includes deploying military aircraft.
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said cyber incidents such as the PHP outage would become more common as AI made it easier to find ways to thwart traditional defences.
He also cited risks from hostile states, organised criminals and climate change.
The UK was facing a greater level of threat "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime", he said during an appearance on the BBC's "Question Time" programme broadcast overnight.
Britain's advice is similar to that issued by the European Commission, which told EU citizens last year to keep a 72-hour emergency kit containing supplies such as food, water, cash and power banks. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CelcomDigi files RM10bil sukuk programme to refinance debt, fund expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd's wholly owned CelcomDigi Telecommunications Sdn Bhd has filed an Islamic medium-term notes programme of up to RM10 billion with the Securities Commission.
The perpetual-tenure sukuk programme will be issued under the Shariah principle of Murabahah via a Tawarruq arrangement and has been assigned a AAA rating by RAM Rating Services Bhd.
Proceeds will be used to finance capital expenditure, working capital, general funding needs and corporate purposes of the issuer, its subsidiaries and the CelcomDigi group.
The funds may also refinance existing conventional borrowings and Islamic financings, finance future Islamic issuances (including redeeming sukuk issued under the programme - and cover related fees and expenses, CelcomDigi said in a bourse filing today.
CelcomDigi said all proceeds from sukuk issued under the programme must be applied towards Shariah-compliant purposes.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd have been appointed joint principal advisers, joint lead arrangers and joint lead managers. AmBank Islamic Bhd and CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd are the joint Shariah advisers.
The proposed programme comes as CelcomDigi's borrowings continue to rise.
Total loans and borrowings stood at RM14.46 billion as of June 30, 2026, up from RM13.85 billion at end-December 2025, while cash and cash equivalents amounted to RM684 million.
For the first half ended June 30, 2026, CelcomDigi posted a net profit of RM816 million, down 2.8 per cent from RM823 million a year earlier.
Its revenue was broadly unchanged at RM6.39 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wawasan leaves Melaka seat allocation to PN leadership
Article:
KOTA BARU: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) is leaving it to the Perikatan Nasional leadership to decide how many seats the party will contest in next month's Melaka election.
Wawasan president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin said the party, as a PN component, would accept whatever decision was made.
"As part of PN, we leave it to the PN chairman (Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar), who has mandated his secretary-general, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, to handle discussions on seat allocation.
"There should not be too many voices. Whatever is decided, we will accept it. We will wait for the PN secretary-general to announce how many seats we will contest," he told a press conference here.
Yesterday, Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi confirmed that seat negotiations with Pas for the Melaka state election had been finalised.
He said BN would contest 21 state seats, while Pas and its allies would contest seven.
On the logo to be used in the Melaka election, Hamzah said Wawasan was considering contesting under the PN logo.
"If possible, we want to use the PN logo. That is why, when we received the letter from the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS), we immediately took the matter to court.
"This shows that we believe PN is the symbol that represents all of us as component parties in the coalition.
"However, discussions are still ongoing to determine the best option," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: First Russian diesel from Putin-Trump deal heading for US, data shows
Article:
NEW YORK: The first Russian diesel bound for the US following a surprise agreement reached between Moscow and US President Donald Trump is aboard a tanker heading for New York, ship-tracking data showed on Friday.
Trump announced the dealthis month as part of his efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of November 3 US mid-term elections.
Trump also waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia and threatened Europe with a US diesel export ban unless countries released more from their emergency reserves to help ease prices.
The Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes was loaded with 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel in Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk on Oct 22, according to LSEG shipping data.
It is expected to arrive in the United States on Nov 7.
The identity of the buyer and seller were not immediately known. The cargo will be the first imported by the US since former President Joe Biden announced a ban on US imports of Russian oil and petroleum products in 2022.
Trump announced on October 9 that Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter."
A Kremlin spokesperson on Friday confirmed a first ship under the deal had departed, but did not specify whether it was bound for the US market or elsewhere.
"As far as I'm aware, there have already been reports from the Ministry of Energy that the first tanker has, in fact, set sail for its recipients, its buyers.
Further shipments will continue at a steady pace from here on," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on a daily conference call.
The deal with the US involved Russia lifting a self-imposed ban on diesel exports.
Russia resuming global exports
Since the EU imposed a full embargo on imports of Russian oil products in Feb 2023 over the war in Ukraine, Russia has exported diesel mainly to Turkey and Brazil, as well as to African countries.
It also supplies Central Asia by rail.
Shipping data from LSEG and Kpler published this week showed Russian diesel cargoes resuming voyages to their traditional destinations after Moscow lifted its own ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil.
It was unclear where other tankers were destined for, with cargoes loaded in Primorsk signalling Gibraltar, the Atlantic Coast or Port-Said, LSEG data showed.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has said additional US shipments would follow as companies from the two countries work out the necessary contracts.
Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who also heads Russia's sovereign wealth fund, said last week that the US Treasury had asked the fund to help sort out tricky payment issues relating to the agreement.
Novak has said that Russia would be able to increase its diesel exports to its usual levels of 3-3.5 million tons per month by year-end. — REUTERS

Title: UK Royal Navy sailor appears in court charged under National Security Act
Article:
LONDON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - A junior member of Britain's Royal Navy accused of collecting secret information and researching a website linked to Russia's foreign intelligence service appeared in a London court on Friday charged under the National Security Act.
Teddy Young is charged with having "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information" between November 2024 and May 2025.
Young's role in the Royal Navy related to "warfare intelligence", prosecutors said at his first appearance earlier this month.
The 24-year-old was allegedly "interested in a website set up by a foreign intelligence service", prosecutor Kelly Brocklehurst said at London's Old Bailey court on Friday.
"The website that he appears to have taken a particular interest in is the foreign intelligence service of Russia, the SVR," Brocklehurst added.
Young, who appeared by video link from Belmarsh prison, is charged with five offences, including two under the National Security Act and one count of misconduct in public office.
He was not asked to enter any pleas and his trial was provisionally listed to begin in October 2027.
Police previously said the charges were not connected to the recent, ongoing investigation into an incident at the RAF Fairford airbase, from where US bombers had carried out strikes on Iran before they were withdrawn.

Title: Valvoline rolls out new motorcycle oils
Article:
VALVOLINE Global Operations has launched a new motorcycle engine oil range in Malaysia, covering four-stroke motorcycles and scooters used for daily commuting and long-distance travel.
The Valvoline Champ range comprises fully synthetic, synthetic-blend and conventional formulations, with different grades designed for varying engine requirements and riding conditions.
The flagship Champ 4T Ultra Racing 10W-50 is a fully synthetic oil aimed at high-performance motorcycles and long-distance riding.
Another key product, the Champ 4T Extra 15W-50, targets riders navigating frequent stop-start urban traffic.
The wider motorcycle range includes Champ 4T Ultra Racing 10W-40, Champ 4T Extra in 10W-40 and 15W-50 grades, and Champ 4T Premium in 20W-40 and 20W-50 grades.
For scooters, the lineup includes the fully synthetic Champ 4T Ultra Scooter 5W-40, alongside Champ 4T Extra Scooter and Champ 4T Premium Scooter in selected 10W-30 and 10W-40 grades.
The products carry relevant American Petroleum Institute (API) performance classifications and Japanese Automotive Standards Organisation (JASO) specifications, including MA2 for motorcycles and MB for scooters.
Valvoline Ccuster manager for Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei Leong Tak Chuan said the range was developed to address local riding conditions, including tropical temperatures and heavy traffic.
The products are distributed in Malaysia by Vanli Group and are available through authorised workshops, retailers and service centres nationwide.
As part of the launch, Vanli Group is sponsoring 1,000 bottles of engine oil for Lalamove driver partners.
Valvoline Global operates in more than 140 countries, with a distribution network spanning over 80,000 locations.
The company is part of Saudi Aramco.

Title: Yinson Production, PTSC achieve first oil at Lac Da Vang field ahead of schedule

The floating storage and offloading (FSO) vessel, FSO PTSC LDV, achieved the milestone on Sept 27, 2026, ahead of the previously communicated fourth-quarter 2026 schedule, it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
Yinson Production chief executive officer Flemming Guiducci Grønnegaard said the achievement reflects the strong collaboration, technical excellence and shared commitment to safety among Yinson Production, joint venture partner PTSC, and its client, Murphy Oil Corporation.

The field's development is expected to ramp up through 2028 as additional wells are brought online, providing a vital new source of production to support Vietnam's growing energy sector.
FSO PTSC LDV is chartered to Murphy Cuu Long Bac Oil Co Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Murphy Oil Corporation, under a 10-year firm contract with extension options of up to five additional years.

Title: DXN breaks ground on its first North African plant in Morocco
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DXN Holdings Bhd has begun construction of its first manufacturing facility in North Africa, in Meknes, Morocco following approval from the Moroccan authorities.
The vertically integrated global wellness manufacturer said the project received its construction permit, and work is now underway at the Agropolis Industrial Park.
"DXN is now working with the government of Morocco to finalise a definitive investment agreement, which will set out the investment subsidies and incentives for the project," it said in a statement.
The memorandum of understanding between its subsidiary, Dexin Morocco SA, and Morocco's Ministry of Industry and Trade and Ministry of Investment, Convergence and Evaluation of Public Policies concluded on Oct 2.
DXN group chief executive officer Prajith Pavithran said the project had progressed from an initial agreement to an approved development with construction underway.
"Our first manufacturing plant in North Africa is a major step in DXN's global growth, and Morocco is central to how we will serve North Africa, Europe and the Middle East in the years ahead," said Prajith.
The facility, which will be built on an 80,765-square-metre site, will manufacture Spirulina and Ganoderma-based products, two of the company's core product lines.
The plant is expected to create about 250 jobs and serve as a regional production hub for markets across North Africa and Europe, complementing DXN's existing manufacturing facility in the Middle East.
The Morocco project forms part of the company's strategy to strengthen control over its value chain, from raw-material production to consumers, while bringing manufacturing closer to its markets.
DXN plans to increase its manufacturing network from 14 factories currently to 21.
For the financial year ending February 28, 2027, the group has allocated capital expenditure of up to RM500 million to expand manufacturing capacity in Malaysia, Brazil, Morocco, Peru and Bolivia.
The allocation will also support plantation initiatives in Bolivia, Brazil and Malaysia to strengthen raw-material security, as well as market development in new and underpenetrated markets, particularly in Africa and Europe.
Prajith said the Morocco facility would improve product accessibility for consumers while supporting shorter supply lines, lower costs and better quality control.
"With construction underway in Meknes and the continued support of the Moroccan authorities, we look forward to completing the plant," he added.

Title: Man jailed 9 years for fatal wrong-way Federal Highway crash that killed 2 teens
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 29-year-old businessman initially charged with murdering two teenagers in a fatal 2021 Federal Highway crash was sentenced to nine years' jail today after pleading guilty to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
The Shah Alam High Court amended the two murder charges against K. Devaaswin to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(b) of the Penal Code after the prosecution closed its case.
Devaaswin was initially charged under Section 302 of the same code, which carries the death penalty, over the deaths of Muhammad Hafiz Syamir Dzul Asri, 19, and Nur Afiqah Abdul Karim, 18.
The teenagers were killed when their car was struck by a four-wheel-drive vehicle driven against the flow of traffic by Devaaswin at Km8.6 of the Federal Highway, heading towards Kuala Lumpur from Klang, at 1.50am on Sept 12, 2021.
Lawyer Datuk N. Sivananthan said his client had maintained from the outset that there was no intention or knowledge to cause death.
"At the end of the prosecution's case, the judge agreed with us and reduced the charge.
"My client did not hesitate and was more than happy to plead guilty to the amended charge," he said.
Sivananthan said Devaaswin was relieved by the decision and accepted that he had to be punished for the deaths, but the sentence had to be proportionate to the offence.
High Court judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet sentenced Devaaswin to nine years' jail on each charge, with both terms to run concurrently from his arrest on Sept 17, 2021.
He was also fined RM30,000 for each charge, with one year's jail in default of payment for each fine.
Sivananthan said that, after the one-third remission applicable to the sentence, his client would serve six years and had about 10 months left to serve.
He said Devaaswin's family would arrange to pay the RM60,000 in fines and hoped to raise the funds before his release.
Devaaswin, previously held at Sungai Buloh Prison, has been transferred to Kajang Prison, he added.
Sivananthan appeared with Nabila Habib, while deputy public prosecutor Mohd Hafizi Abdul Halim prosecuted.

Title: Federal Court to hear former Negri Sembilan exco dismissal challenge on Dec 16
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court will hear on Dec 16 a legal challenge by 10 former Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members against the state ruler's decision to revoke their appointments last month.
Lawyer Datuk Wira Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the former exco members, and lawyer Marisa Regina Mohd Aris Rizal, representing the Negri Sembilan government, confirmed the hearing date after case management before Deputy Registrar Azaraorni Abd Rahman.
The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
They filed the notice of motion on Oct 14 and named the Negri Sembilan State Secretary and the state government as respondents.
Through the application, they are seeking the Federal Court's determination on three legal questions concerning the interpretation and effect of provisions in the Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959.
The questions arose from an originating summons they filed at the Seremban High Court.
On Oct 5, they filed the originating summons to challenge the validity of the gazette notification revoking their appointments as state exco members.
One question is whether Article 38(5), read together with Articles 38(2), 38(3), 38(4), 40(1), 40(1A) and 40(2) of the state constitution, authorises the Yang Dipertuan Besar to revoke an exco member's appointment without the advice of the menteri besar.
If the answer is no, they want the court to determine whether the revocation, gazetted on Sept 24, was constitutional and whether it is null, void and without legal effect.
Another question is whether Article 38(5), read with Article 28(1), means that the term Raja Pemerintah (Ruler) refers to the Yang Dipertuan Besar, giving him the discretion to revoke an exco member's appointment without the menteri besar's advice.
If the answer is no, the court must determine whether the former exco members' dismissal contravened the state constitution.
On Sept 20, the Negri Sembilan palace announced that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of the 10 exco members with immediate effect.
The revocation was gazetted on Sept 24, with their removal taking effect from Sept 20.
The gazette stated that their appointments were revoked and annulled because they had breached their pledge of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz by agreeing to his removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Title: Homestay turned scam hub in Melaka, 34 arrested
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has raided a homestay used as a call centre to defraud South Koreans through fake investment schemes, arresting 34 people.
The syndicate is believed to have been operating for three months, using social media platforms and messaging applications to lure victims with investment schemes promising high returns within a short period.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation yesterday also led to the arrest of two local men who allegedly received RM3,000 to guard the premises and supervise the workers.
"Those arrested comprised 31 people from China, including 29 men and two women, a Taiwanese man and two local men, aged between 20 and 51.
"Initial checks found that three Chinese men had overstayed their permits, while the other foreigners did not have valid travel documents or passes to remain in the country," he said in a statement.
Zakaria said the operation was conducted by officers from the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission in Cyberjaya and the state Immigration Department, following a month of intelligence gathering.
"The syndicate used a homestay as its operational base to avoid detection by the authorities.
"Investigations found that its operators were assigned three main roles: handling customer service, managing investment-related information and maintaining customer data.
"The operators were also allegedly prohibited from leaving the premises throughout their working hours, with food delivered by the two local men. The syndicate operated from 8am to 8pm daily," he said.
Zakaria said items seized during the raid included 309 mobile phones, 45 computers, five routers, a gigabit switch, a portable WiFi device, three Chinese passports, a gate remote control and 21 notebooks containing instructions on how to defraud victims.
The total value of the seized items was estimated at RM318,600.
"The two local men were detained for suspected offences under Section 56(1)(d) of the Immigration Act, while the foreigners were detained for suspected offences under Sections 6(1)(c) and 15(1)(c) of the same Act," he said.
Those detained were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further investigation.

Title: MCMC investigates Facebook’s failure to block livestream of teacher attack in Kuching, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating Facebook’s failure to detect or block a livestream of an attack on a teacher in Kuching, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The Madani government spokesperson said he would leave it to MCMC to investigate the incident before making any further comments.
He said the failure of social media platforms to prevent the livestreaming of violent acts was not new, with similar incidents having occurred in several other countries.
“MCMC is currently investigating the matter. We have seen similar cases in other countries where platforms have failed to prevent violent acts from being livestreamed.
“So, I will leave it to MCMC to investigate and issue a statement in due course,” he told a press conference here today.
He was responding to a question on whether the government had sought an explanation from Meta over Facebook’s failure to detect or block the livestream from the outset.
On Wednesday, a 16-year-old male student allegedly attacked a female teacher with an axe at an international school in Kuching, leaving the victim with injuries to her hand.
Sarawak Acting Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said the case was being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi tells LLM, Prosignal to explain TuJu app glitches and fixes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 23 — The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd have been asked to provide a detailed explanation of problems affecting users of the local navigation app TuJu, including their causes, technical issues and corrective measures.
Madani Government spokesman and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said LLM had acknowledged the problems and confirmed that improvements were under way.
“The explanation from LLM and Prosignal is crucial to addressing users' concerns comprehensively, improving TuJu's reliability and strengthening public confidence in the local navigation app,” he told a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today.
Fahmi also encouraged the public to consider alternative navigation apps developed by both local and foreign companies.
“What matters is avoiding Waze due to the security concerns highlighted by the National Security Council,” he said.
Last Tuesday, the government encouraged Malaysians to use TuJu, developed by LLM, as an alternative navigation app.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the recommendation followed concerns over information security and users' movement data, citing Waze's links to Israeli law.
TuJu was developed by Prosignal Consortium under a memorandum of understanding signed with LLM on May 26, 2022, and officially launched on November 26, 2025. — Bernama

Title: Anwar apologises over Waze ban linked to Israel, says national security comes first (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has apologised if the decision to ban a navigation application owned by an entity linked to the Israeli regime causes any inconvenience to the public.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said this firm measure had to be taken to ensure the security of the nation and its people, a matter that cannot be compromised under any circumstances.
“I apologise if the decision to ban this navigation application, which belongs to the Israeli regime, causes inconvenience to the public.
“However, the security of the nation and its people cannot be compromised, as we must uphold national sovereignty and protect the personal information of our citizens,” he said.
Earlier, the prime minister indicated that the government has not ruled out the possibility of a complete ban on the use of the navigation application Waze in Malaysia.
He noted that such a move could be considered once the government has evaluated alternatives to Waze, including the potential for local development of a similar, fully functional application.
Last Wednesday, the government decided to prohibit all civil servants from using the navigation application Waze, in order to safeguard government information and users' personal data against the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime. — Bernama
